To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gangliosidoses are caused by a deficiency in a lysosomal enzyme, and that the gangliosis is caused by the accumulation of the substrate of this enzyme.
Gangliosides are enriched in a light subcellular membrane fraction of rat brain.

ganglioside-enriched light membranes from neonatal rat brain are enriched in glycosphingoglycolipid, protein, and ganglioside, but are depleted in cholesterol, phospholipoprotein, and neutral glycolipids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of a light membrane fraction enriched with gangliosides and with the determination of the composition of these ganglioside-enriched fractions.
the isolation of a light membrane fraction of developing rat brain which is enriched in gangliiosides relative to protein, and with a study of its properties.
the study of the biosynthesis of ganglioside in the developing rat brain and the isolation and characterization of the gangliosidic fractions from different regions of the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gangliosidic material is not confined to any one subcellular fraction, but is found in all subcellular fractions, including myelin.
the gangliosidic content of the light membrane is not a constant feature of the fraction but depends upon the conditions under which it is prepared.
the gangliosidic content of a given subcellular fraction is determined by the following factors: (a) The relative amounts of ganglioside and protein in the fraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the gangliosidic content of the light membrane fractions from adult rat brain is not due to the presence of myelinated axons but to the presence of a membrane system in which the gangliosidoses are synthesized and stored.
the gangliosidic content in the brain of the newborn rat increases in parallel with the development of neuronal structures.

we have shown that the deposition of the gangliosidic material is a premyelin process, and that the subcellular distribution of ganglioside in the brain of the rat is not the same in the neonate and adult.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is a very complex organ.

the gangliosidic content of the light membrane fractions from both adult and developing rat brains is not due to contamination with myelin, and that these fractions are enriched in ganglioses relative to other membrane constituents, such as phospholipid, cholesterol, and protein.
the gangliosidic composition of the developing brain is very different from the mature brain, and the gangliosids are not evenly distributed throughout the brain.
